Kata / a first usable practice

Give the content
its proper place.

One focus. Equal alternatives. A lead with support. Start with what a slide should communicate, then choose its scale, alignment and space.

This working example recomposes seven slides from a real supplier briefing. The supplied wording and order stay intact. The explanations below connect each choice to what you can see.

01 / techUk Event · source slide 1

Crown Commercial Service · 25 February 202001 / 07

techUk Event

25 February 2020

Historical excerpt · source slide 1 · Crown copyright / Open Government Licence

The event title stands alone with its date. Open space gives the short title presence without inventing an additional message.

Alternative. A centered title would be quieter; the left alignment gives the briefing a direct opening.

02 / Introducing Crown Commercial Service · source slide 3

Crown Commercial Service · 25 February 202002 / 07

Introducing Crown Commercial Service

We help organisations across the entire public sector save time and money on buying their everyday goods and services…

  • Commercial expertise
  • Supporting frontline services
  • Significant savings
  • Customer focused
  • Bulk buying power

We aim to help our customers save £2 billion between 2016 and 2020

Historical excerpt · source slide 3 · Crown copyright / Open Government Licence

The supplied purpose receives the larger field. The five supporting capabilities share a quieter adjacent field; the dated ambition remains explicit beneath both.

Alternative. A vertical stack allows longer lines, but separates the purpose from its supporting capabilities.

View this slide ↗

03 / Why G-Cloud? · source slide 5

Crown Commercial Service · 25 February 202003 / 07

Why G-Cloud?

  • A competitive marketplace for huge range of cloud solutions
  • Framework’s re-procured every 12 months to keep services fresh
  • Cloud First, Government determined to be as efficient as possible
  • A catalogue of commoditised, cloud based services
  • Fast procurement process
Historical excerpt · source slide 5 · Crown copyright / Open Government Licence

A shared left edge and generous line spacing keep five supplied reasons readable as a single group. None is promoted as the decisive reason.

Alternative. A multi-column layout would shorten the lines but fragment this modest list.

View this slide ↗

04 / G-Cloud Background · source slide 6

Crown Commercial Service · 25 February 202004 / 07

G-Cloud Background

  • Over 4,000 suppliers
  • Nearly 30,000 services
  • Nearly 90% of the suppliers are SME’s
  • £5.7 billion spend on G-Cloud since 2012
  • Over 40% of spend goes to SME’s
  • In 2019 1467 suppliers reported spend
Historical excerpt · source slide 6 · Crown copyright / Open Government Licence

Six complete statements share equal treatment in two open columns. Qualifiers stay in the statements rather than becoming tiny footnotes below oversized numbers.

Alternative. A single vertical list preserves an even simpler reading order but gives each statement less presence.

View this slide ↗

05 / G-Cloud Vs DOS · source slide 8

Crown Commercial Service · 25 February 202005 / 07

G-Cloud Vs DOS

G-Cloud

  • Utility cloud services
  • Contract award (after 6 step buying process)
  • Supplier T&Cs
  • Supplier IPR/Source code
  • No Agile development (configuration only)

DOS

  • Bespoke services
  • Further competition
  • Government T&Cs
  • Customer IPR/Source code
  • Agile development - iterative
Historical excerpt · source slide 8 · Crown copyright / Open Government Licence

Equal fields, matching titles and aligned rows make the supplied comparison visible without a preferred option. Open gutters replace the two differently coloured source panels.

Alternative. Equal stacked rows give longer lines on narrow screens but lose simultaneous comparison.

06 / What services can you sell through G-Cloud 12? · source slide 13

Crown Commercial Service · 25 February 202006 / 07

What services can you sell through G-Cloud 12?

1

Cloud Hosting

Covers Infrastructure and Platform as a Service for example a computer server or storage in the cloud

2

Cloud Software

Is an application or service that can be run over the internet or cloud for example accounting tools or customer service management software

3

Cloud Support

Support your transition to IaaS, PaaS and SaaS for example migration to the cloud, configuration/implementation of services from Lots 1 & 2

Historical excerpt · source slide 13 · Crown copyright / Open Government Licence

Three rows preserve the supplied numbered service groups. The labels align at left and the descriptions get a consistent, longer measure at right.

Alternative. Three columns would make each service feel self-contained but wrap these descriptions into narrow blocks.

View this slide ↗

07 / Questions & Answers · source slide 21

Crown Commercial Service · 25 February 202007 / 07

Questions & Answers

Historical excerpt · source slide 21 · Crown copyright / Open Government Licence

The closing subject has the same restrained treatment as the opening. Empty space leaves attention on the discussion.

Alternative. A smaller centered treatment would feel more reflective; matching the opening keeps the brief visually consistent.
